questions.q: When she was young, she ___ run very fast.
questions.why: Use 'could' for general ability in the past.

questions.q: I'm sorry, I ___ swim. I never learned.
questions.why: 'Can't' expresses lack of ability in the present.

questions.q: You ___ wear a seatbelt; it's the law here.
questions.why: 'Must' expresses strong obligation, often a rule or law.

questions.q: Everyone ___ have a passport to cross the border.
questions.why: 'Have to' expresses obligation that comes from outside rules or circumstances.

questions.q: You ___ smoke in the hospital; it is strictly forbidden.
questions.why: 'Mustn't' means it is prohibited to do something.

questions.q: It's Sunday, so you ___ get up early. Sleep in!
questions.why: 'Don't have to' means there is no obligation, not a prohibition.

questions.q: You look exhausted. You ___ get some rest.
questions.why: 'Should' is used to give advice.

questions.q: You ___ to apologize to her for being so rude.
questions.why: 'Ought to' gives advice and is always followed by 'to'.

questions.q: He's been working all day. He ___ be very tired now.
questions.why: 'Must' expresses a confident logical deduction.

questions.q: That ___ be John at the door; he's in Australia right now.
questions.why: 'Can't' expresses certainty that something is impossible.

questions.q: I'm not sure where she is. She ___ be at the library.
questions.why: 'Might' expresses a possibility you are unsure about.

questions.q: ___ you pass me the salt, please?
questions.why: 'Could' makes a polite request.

questions.q: ___ I use your phone for a moment?
questions.why: 'May I' is a polite way to ask for permission.

questions.q: You ___ have told me earlier; now it's too late.
questions.why: 'Should have' criticizes a past action that did not happen.

questions.q: The ground is wet. It ___ have rained last night.
questions.why: 'Must have' expresses a confident deduction about the past.

questions.q: She didn't answer. She ___ have been asleep.
questions.why: 'Could have' expresses a past possibility.

questions.q: He failed the exam, but he ___ have passed if he had studied.
questions.why: 'Could have' describes a past possibility that didn't happen.

questions.q: You ___ worry about the bill; I've already paid it.
questions.why: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary to do something.

questions.q: When I was a child, I ___ speak French fluently, but now I've forgotten it.
questions.why: 'Could' describes ability in the past.

questions.q: They ___ be home; all the lights are off.
questions.why: 'Can't' expresses a confident negative deduction about the present.

questions.q: You ___ have eaten so much cake; that's why you feel sick now.
questions.why: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes a past action that was a mistake.

questions.q: In my country, children ___ go to school until they are sixteen.
questions.why: 'Have to' expresses external obligation such as a law.

questions.q: I ___ to finish this report by Friday or my boss will be angry.
questions.why: 'Have to' expresses obligation and is followed by 'to'.

questions.q: ___ you mind closing the window? It's cold.
questions.why: 'Would you mind' is a polite way to make a request.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'It's a secret, so you ___ tell anyone.' (prohibition)
questions.why: 'Mustn't' expresses prohibition.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'You ___ have called me; I would have helped you.' (past advice/regret)
questions.why: 'Should have' expresses regret about something not done in the past.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Tomorrow is a holiday, so we ___ have to work.' (no obligation, negative)
questions.why: 'Don't have to' means there is no obligation.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She studied hard, so she ___ pass the exam easily.' (deduction of certainty)
questions.why: 'Must' expresses a confident logical conclusion.

questions.q: Type the answer: '___ I leave early today, please?' (polite permission)
questions.why: 'May', 'could', or 'can' can request permission.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'When I was ten, I ___ ride a bike without help.' (past ability)
questions.why: 'Could' is used for ability in the past.

questions.q: You ___ smoke in here — it's forbidden.
questions.why: 'Mustn't' = prohibition; 'don't have to' = no obligation.

questions.q: You ___ pay — the entrance is free.
questions.why: 'Don't have to' = it is not necessary.

questions.q: She ___ be home; all the lights are on.
questions.why: 'Must' for a logical deduction based on evidence.

questions.q: ___ I borrow your pen for a moment?
questions.why: 'May' asks for permission politely.

questions.q: You look exhausted. You ___ take a break.
questions.why: 'Should' gives advice.
